title: Microsoft AZ-104: Azure Administrator Practice Test 1

authorship.note: All learner-facing scenarios, answer choices, ordering tasks, and drag/drop-style items in this simulation are original. No leaked exam dumps or proprietary question banks were copied. The design was calibrated from Microsoft's current AZ-104 study guide, official exam-experience documentation, Microsoft Learn product documentation, and the public exam sandbox/question-type guidance.

official_exam_reference.note: Microsoft does not publish a fixed AZ-104 item count or a fixed count of unscored items. Microsoft states that exam item counts can vary and that some items may be unscored. This simulation uses 50 total items and hides 5 authored unscored items to reproduce that behavior without claiming those counts are official. Raw practice-test percentage is not equivalent to Microsoft's scaled score.

practice_test_behavior.recommended_review: Review incorrect answers and low-confidence answers after submission.

format_basis: AZ-104 certification page currently lists 100 minutes for the assessment.

Microsoft says certification exams may include traditional question types such as multiple choice, drag-and-drop/build-list style items, case studies, and possibly labs; Microsoft does not guarantee a specific item-type mix in advance.
This JSON cannot reproduce a live Azure lab, so hands-on behavior is approximated with configuration assignment, ordering, and scenario questions.
Longer case-study-style items are mixed with focused operational questions to create exam-like reading density without copying exam content.

validation.cargo_execution: not_available_in_current_environment; validated against current Rust source contracts instead

factual_review.source_policy: Every item includes the current AZ-104 study guide plus at least one relevant Microsoft Learn product/documentation reference.

notes: Selection-heavy items are intentional because Microsoft role-based exams use traditional selection questions, while ordering/classification/configuration items approximate build-list and drag/drop interactions supported by the app.
The test does not claim to reproduce a live Azure lab.
Authored directly for the repository practice-test-v2 schema; no schema migration was required.

question.prompt: A project team from a partner company needs access to a SharePoint-connected Azure application that uses your Microsoft Entra tenant for authentication. The partner users must continue using credentials managed by their own organization. What should the Azure administrator do?
question.explanation: Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration lets external users authenticate with identities managed by their home organization while being represented as guest users in the resource tenant.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?

choices.label: Create local member accounts for each partner user and assign temporary passwords.
Invite the partner users as B2B guest users in the tenant.
Create a managed identity for each partner user.
Add the partner domain as an Azure DNS zone.

choice_feedback.A: Local member accounts would make your tenant manage the credentials.
choice_feedback.B: Correct. B2B guest collaboration fits external organizational users.
choice_feedback.C: Managed identities are for workloads, not human partner users.
choice_feedback.D: Azure DNS does not create identities or grant application access.

question.prompt: An application must grant a client temporary access to blobs without sharing the storage account key. The administrator wants the authorization to be based on a Microsoft Entra identity where possible. Which TWO statements are correct?
question.explanation: A user delegation SAS for Blob Storage is authorized with Microsoft Entra credentials, and SAS tokens should follow least-privilege scope and lifetime practices.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Grant limited access to data with shared access signatures (SAS)

choices.label: A user delegation SAS can be secured with Microsoft Entra credentials.
A storage account key must be embedded in the client for every SAS design.
A SAS should be scoped to the minimum permissions and shortest practical lifetime.
A resource lock can replace a SAS token for data-plane access.
A management group controls the SAS signature.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. User delegation SAS uses Microsoft Entra authorization for the delegation key.
choice_feedback.B: A SAS can be issued without exposing the account key to the client.
choice_feedback.C: Correct. Minimize permissions, resources, and validity period.
choice_feedback.D: Locks protect management operations and do not grant blob data access.
choice_feedback.E: Management groups do not sign SAS tokens.

question.prompt: A Bicep file contains the same storage account SKU value in three resource declarations. The team wants callers to choose the SKU at deployment time without editing the file. What should you add and reference?
question.explanation: A Bicep parameter exposes a value to the deployment caller. Replacing repeated hard-coded values with a parameter makes the template reusable without editing the source.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
What is Bicep?

choices.label: A parameter for the SKU value.
A deployment slot.
A resource lock.
A Network Security Group rule.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Parameters are deployment-time inputs.
choice_feedback.B: Deployment slots are an App Service feature.
choice_feedback.C: A lock protects resources from changes.
choice_feedback.D: NSG rules control network traffic.

Virtual network peering

question.prompt: A VM CPU metric shows short spikes every morning. The operations team wants an alert only when average CPU remains above a threshold for multiple evaluation periods. Which Azure capability should they configure?
question.explanation: Azure Monitor metric alerts evaluate metric time series using configured aggregation, threshold, frequency, and window criteria.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Azure Monitor overview
Overview of Azure Monitor alerts

choices.label: An Azure Monitor metric alert with the required aggregation, threshold, and evaluation settings.
A Blob stored access policy.
A Recovery Services vault lock.
A VNet peering connection.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Metric alerts are designed for this time-series condition.
choice_feedback.B: Stored access policies manage SAS behavior.
choice_feedback.C: Backup vault configuration does not monitor CPU.
choice_feedback.D: VNet peering provides connectivity.

question.prompt: Users report that the Self-service password reset link is available, but a specific pilot user cannot complete a reset because the service says the user is not enabled for SSPR. SSPR is configured for a selected group. What should you check first?
question.explanation: When SSPR is scoped to selected users or groups, the user must be included in that scope before the reset experience is enabled for that account.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
How Microsoft Entra self-service password reset works

choices.label: Whether the user is a member of the group targeted by the SSPR configuration.
Whether the user has the Owner role on the subscription.
Whether the user has a public IP address assigned.
Whether the tenant has an Azure Policy assignment.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Scope membership is the direct control for a selected-group deployment.
choice_feedback.B: Azure subscription ownership does not enable SSPR.
choice_feedback.C: Network public IP assignment is unrelated to Entra SSPR eligibility.
choice_feedback.D: Azure Policy governs Azure resources, not SSPR scope.

question.prompt: An application currently authenticates to Azure Storage with key1. Arrange the safest key-rotation sequence to avoid downtime.
question.explanation: Use the second valid key while regenerating the first, move the application to the regenerated first key, and then regenerate the second key. Two keys exist to support rotation without an outage.

question.instruction: Arrange the items in the correct order.

items.label: Regenerate key1

question.prompt: Two peered VNets use non-overlapping address spaces. VM1 in VNet-A cannot reach VM2 in VNet-B after an administrator added a route table to VM1's subnet. The effective route now sends the destination prefix to a virtual appliance that is not forwarding the traffic. What should you fix first?
question.explanation: Effective routes determine the next hop. A user-defined route that captures the destination prefix can divert traffic away from the peering path, so the route is the first issue to correct.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Azure virtual network traffic routing
Virtual network peering

choices.label: Correct or remove the user-defined route that overrides the expected path.
Create a Blob lifecycle policy.
Add a resource lock to VNet-B.
Regenerate a storage account key.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. The evidence directly identifies the wrong next hop.
choice_feedback.B: Blob lifecycle is unrelated to VNet routing.
choice_feedback.C: A resource lock does not repair packet routing.
choice_feedback.D: Storage keys do not affect VNet reachability.

question.prompt: An operations team needs Contributor access only to resources in RG-Prod. The same subscription also contains RG-Finance, which the team must not change. At which scope should you create the role assignment?
question.explanation: A resource-group scope grants the role to resources in that group through inheritance while avoiding access to sibling resource groups. Assigning individually would work but is unnecessarily granular.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Understand scope for Azure RBAC
What is Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC)?

choices.label: Management group
Subscription
RG-Prod resource group
Each individual resource in RG-Prod only

choice_feedback.A: A management-group assignment would be much broader.
choice_feedback.B: A subscription assignment would include RG-Finance.
choice_feedback.C: Correct. This is the narrowest convenient scope that covers all resources in RG-Prod.
choice_feedback.D: Per-resource assignments are more administrative work than necessary for the stated requirement.

question.prompt: An administrator wants resource logs from a storage account to be queryable with KQL in a Log Analytics workspace, and critical alerts should notify an operations team. Which TWO configurations are directly involved?
question.explanation: Diagnostic settings route supported platform logs and metrics to destinations such as Log Analytics. Alert rules can use action groups to deliver notifications or trigger actions.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor
Log queries in Azure Monitor
Overview of Azure Monitor alerts
Action groups in Azure Monitor

choices.label: A diagnostic setting that sends the selected resource logs to the Log Analytics workspace.
An action group connected to the relevant alert rule.
A Blob lifecycle policy.
A VM availability set.
A stored access policy.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. This sends the telemetry to Log Analytics.
choice_feedback.B: Correct. Action groups define notification/action targets for alerts.
choice_feedback.C: Lifecycle policies manage Blob data age/tiering.
choice_feedback.D: Availability sets affect VM placement.
choice_feedback.E: Stored access policies manage SAS authorization.

question.prompt: A storage account should reject traffic from the public internet except for requests that originate from a specific Azure virtual network subnet. Which storage security configuration is the direct fit?
question.explanation: Storage account network rules can restrict access to selected virtual networks and subnets. Data authorization still applies separately.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Secure your Azure Storage account

choices.label: Allow network access from all networks and rely only on blob container ACLs.
Configure the storage account network rules to allow selected virtual networks/subnets.
Regenerate both storage account keys.
Enable blob versioning.

choice_feedback.A: Public network access from all networks does not meet the network restriction.
choice_feedback.B: Correct. Storage firewalls and virtual-network rules enforce the network boundary.
choice_feedback.C: Key rotation changes credentials, not network reachability.
choice_feedback.D: Versioning protects data history, not network access.

question.prompt: You are troubleshooting whether TCP 443 traffic from VM-A can reach VM-B across Azure networking. Which TWO Network Watcher capabilities are directly useful for validating the path or connectivity?
question.explanation: Network Watcher provides connectivity troubleshooting and Connection Monitor for monitoring end-to-end network connectivity.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Troubleshoot network connections with Azure Network Watcher
Connection Monitor overview

choices.label: Connection troubleshoot / connectivity checks.
Connection Monitor.
Blob soft delete.
App Service deployment slots.
Azure Policy remediation.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Connectivity troubleshooting can test the path and identify issues.
choice_feedback.B: Correct. Connection Monitor continuously observes connection health and performance.
choice_feedback.C: Blob soft delete is a data-protection feature.
choice_feedback.D: Deployment slots are an App Service release feature.
choice_feedback.E: Policy remediation is governance, not path testing.

question.prompt: A compliance requirement states that temporary data written between a VM and the storage service, including the host cache, must be encrypted on the VM host. Which VM capability should you evaluate?
question.explanation: Encryption at host encrypts VM data at the host, including supported temp disks and disk caches, before data flows to the storage service.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Encryption at host for Azure virtual machines

choices.label: Encryption at host.
Blob lifecycle management.
Azure DNS alias records.
A ReadOnly resource lock.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. This is the VM feature aimed at host-level data encryption.
choice_feedback.B: Blob lifecycle management applies to Blob Storage tiers and retention.
choice_feedback.C: DNS records do not provide disk encryption.
choice_feedback.D: A resource lock does not encrypt VM data.

question.prompt: A service SAS is associated with a stored access policy on a blob container. A token is discovered in a public log and must be revoked before its stated expiry time. What should you change?
question.explanation: A stored access policy provides a server-side control point for service SAS tokens that reference it. Updating or deleting the policy can invalidate that authorization.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Grant limited access to data with shared access signatures (SAS)
Define a stored access policy

choices.label: Delete or modify the stored access policy associated with the SAS.
Change the blob access tier to Archive.
Enable ZRS on the storage account.
Add a resource tag named Revoked=true.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. The stored access policy is the revocation/control mechanism for the associated service SAS.
choice_feedback.B: Access tier changes do not revoke authorization.
choice_feedback.C: Redundancy does not revoke a SAS.
choice_feedback.D: Tags do not affect data-plane authorization.

question.prompt: A company plans to move a production VM to another subscription. Which TWO checks are appropriate before the move?
question.explanation: Resource moves have prerequisites and support limitations. Administrators should validate move support, subscription/tenant conditions, and dependencies before moving production resources.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Move guidance for virtual machines
What is Azure Resource Manager?

choices.label: Confirm that the source and destination subscriptions are in a supported relationship and that the VM/resource types support the move.
Review dependent resources because some associated resources must be moved together or have restrictions.
Assume every Azure resource can move between any two subscriptions without validation.
Delete the VM before checking move support.
Replace Azure RBAC with Blob SAS tokens.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Move support and subscription conditions must be validated.
choice_feedback.B: Correct. VM-related dependencies can affect move feasibility.
choice_feedback.C: Move support is resource-specific and not universal.
choice_feedback.D: Deletion is not a prerequisite to validation.
choice_feedback.E: Blob SAS is unrelated to Resource Manager moves.

question.prompt: A user has the Contributor role on a resource group and needs to grant Reader access on that same resource group to another user. No other role assignments apply. Can the user perform the role assignment?
question.explanation: Contributor can create and manage Azure resources but cannot assign Azure RBAC roles. A role such as Owner or User Access Administrator is needed to manage access assignments.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Azure built-in roles
What is Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC)?

choices.label: Yes. Contributor can manage both resources and role assignments.
No. Contributor can manage resources but does not grant permission to manage Azure RBAC role assignments.

choice_feedback.A: Contributor explicitly excludes role-assignment management.
choice_feedback.B: Correct. Resource management and access management are separated.

question.prompt: A VM is protected by Azure Backup. Operations needs to restore data after accidental deletion and wants the recovery process governed by the configured backup schedule and retention settings. Which Azure object defines when backups are taken and how long recovery points are retained?
question.explanation: Azure Backup policies define backup schedules and retention for protected workloads. Restore operations use the recovery points produced under those policies.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
What is Azure Backup?
Azure Backup policy

choices.label: The backup policy associated with the protected workload.
The VM network security group.
The VNet route table.
The Azure DNS zone.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Backup policy controls schedule and retention.
choice_feedback.B: NSGs control traffic, not backup retention.
choice_feedback.C: Route tables control next hops.
choice_feedback.D: DNS zones store name-resolution records.

question.prompt: A security policy requires the organization to control the lifecycle of the key used for Azure Storage encryption at rest instead of relying only on Microsoft-managed keys. What should the administrator configure?
question.explanation: Azure Storage encrypts data at rest. A customer-managed key lets the organization control the key lifecycle through an Azure Key Vault or supported key-management configuration.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Azure Storage encryption for data at rest

choices.label: A customer-managed key for the storage account encryption configuration.
A blob snapshot schedule.
A shared access signature with write permission.
An Azure DNS private zone.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. This gives the organization key-management control.
choice_feedback.B: Snapshots protect versions of data, not the encryption-key lifecycle.
choice_feedback.C: SAS grants access and is unrelated to the encryption-at-rest key.
choice_feedback.D: DNS does not select the storage encryption key.

question.prompt: A company is cleaning up Microsoft Entra administration. Which TWO tasks are identity-directory administration tasks rather than Azure resource RBAC tasks?

choice_feedback.B: This is an Azure RBAC assignment.

question.prompt: A storage account must be reachable from an application subnet over a private IP, and the organization wants the storage service to be inaccessible through its public endpoint for this workload. What should you deploy?
question.explanation: A private endpoint assigns a private IP in the virtual network for the PaaS resource. Private DNS is commonly used so the service name resolves to the private endpoint from the VNet.

choices.label: A private endpoint for the storage account and appropriate private DNS configuration.
A service endpoint only, while requiring the application to use a public IP address for storage.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. This provides private-IP connectivity to the PaaS service.
choice_feedback.B: A service endpoint secures service access from a subnet but the PaaS service still uses its public endpoint/addressing model.
choice_feedback.C: Deployment slots do not provide Storage private connectivity.

question.prompt: A production resource group has a CanNotDelete lock. An administrator with the Owner role needs to change a VM size but must not delete the VM. What effect does the lock have?
question.explanation: A CanNotDelete lock permits authorized modification but blocks deletion. Locks apply regardless of Azure RBAC role, including Owner, until the lock is removed.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure

choices.label: The Owner can change the VM size but deletion is blocked until the lock is removed.
The Owner can delete the VM because Owner overrides locks.
The VM becomes read-only and cannot be resized.
The lock blocks sign-in to the VM.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. CanNotDelete protects against deletion while still allowing updates.
choice_feedback.B: Owner does not bypass a Resource Manager lock.
choice_feedback.C: That describes the stronger ReadOnly lock, not CanNotDelete.
choice_feedback.D: Resource locks govern Resource Manager operations, not guest OS sign-in.

question.prompt: A VM must be resized to a SKU that is not available on its current cluster. The resize operation cannot proceed while the VM remains on that hardware cluster. What is the usual next administrative action?
question.explanation: If the requested size is unavailable on the current hardware cluster, deallocating the VM can allow Azure to place it on hardware that supports the new size. A restart is not equivalent to deallocation.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Resize a virtual machine

choices.label: Deallocate the VM, resize it to the supported size, and start it again.
Delete the OS disk and recreate it from scratch.
Convert the VM to an App Service.
Create a stored access policy.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Deallocation can free the placement constraint and allow resizing.
choice_feedback.B: Deleting the OS disk is destructive and unnecessary.
choice_feedback.C: App Service is a different compute service.
choice_feedback.D: Stored access policies are for Storage SAS management.

choice_feedback.B: Correct. The certificate binding enables HTTPS for the hostname.
choice_feedback.C: A Recovery Services vault is unrelated to the App Service HTTPS endpoint.
choice_feedback.D: Blob versioning protects storage data.

question.prompt: A finance team wants an email warning when monthly Azure spending approaches a planned amount. They do not want Azure to automatically stop workloads. What should you configure?
question.explanation: Cost Management budgets can trigger alerts as spending approaches configured thresholds. Budgets do not automatically stop resources.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Plan to manage Azure costs

choices.label: A Cost Management budget with alert thresholds.
A ReadOnly resource lock.
An Azure Policy deny assignment for expensive VM sizes.
A management group deletion lock.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. A budget is the direct cost-threshold notification mechanism.
choice_feedback.B: A lock protects resources from changes; it does not monitor spend.
choice_feedback.C: Policy can restrict configurations but does not implement a spend threshold alert.
choice_feedback.D: A management group is not a spend alert mechanism.

question.prompt: A public Azure Load Balancer distributes TCP traffic to two VMs. Arrange the configuration elements in the logical flow from client-facing entry to backend health-aware distribution.
question.explanation: The frontend receives client traffic. A load-balancing rule maps frontend protocol/port to a backend pool and references a health probe so traffic is sent to healthy instances.

question.prompt: A stateless web tier needs 20 identical VM instances today and must automatically increase or decrease instance count as demand changes. Which Azure compute construct is the best fit?
question.explanation: Virtual Machine Scale Sets are designed to deploy and manage a group of load-balanced VMs and support scaling the number of instances.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets overview

choices.label: Virtual Machine Scale Sets.
A single availability set.
Azure DNS.
A Backup vault.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. VMSS directly addresses identical scalable VM fleets.
choice_feedback.B: An availability set improves availability placement but does not by itself create an autoscaling fleet.
choice_feedback.C: DNS resolves names and does not scale VMs.
choice_feedback.D: Backup vaults protect data and workloads.

question.prompt: Match each recovery requirement to the Azure service or vault type that most directly fits it.
question.explanation: Recovery Services vaults support traditional Azure Backup workloads such as Azure VM backup, Backup vaults support newer Azure Data Protection workloads, and Site Recovery provides disaster-recovery replication and failover.

question.prompt: Azure Policy has a deployIfNotExists assignment that requires a diagnostic setting. Existing resources are already marked noncompliant. You want Policy to create the missing configuration on those existing resources. What should you do?
question.explanation: For effects such as deployIfNotExists or modify, a remediation task can bring existing noncompliant resources toward compliance. Required permissions must also be available to the policy managed identity.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Overview of Azure Policy

choices.label: Create a remediation task for the policy assignment.
Add a CanNotDelete lock to the resources.
Move the resources to another subscription.
Assign Reader to the policy managed identity.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Remediation applies the policy action to existing resources.
choice_feedback.B: A lock does not remediate missing settings.
choice_feedback.C: Moving resources does not add the required setting.
choice_feedback.D: Reader is not sufficient to deploy a missing resource configuration.

question.prompt: You are preparing two storage accounts for Blob object replication. Which TWO settings are required before replication can operate?
question.explanation: Blob object replication requires blob versioning on both accounts and change feed on the source account. It asynchronously replicates eligible block blobs according to the replication policy.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Object replication for block blobs

choices.label: Enable blob versioning on both source and destination accounts.
Enable blob change feed on the source account.
Enable Azure Files soft delete on both accounts.
Use only LRS on both accounts.
Disable all network rules.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Versioning is required on both sides.
choice_feedback.B: Correct. The source change feed drives replication changes.
choice_feedback.C: Azure Files protection is unrelated to Blob object replication.
choice_feedback.D: Object replication is not limited to LRS.
choice_feedback.E: Network rules do not need to be globally disabled.

question.prompt: An Azure Container App should scale out when HTTP demand rises and scale down when demand falls. You do not want to manage a Kubernetes cluster. What should you configure?
question.explanation: Azure Container Apps supports workload-driven scaling rules, including HTTP and event-driven patterns, without requiring the user to operate the underlying Kubernetes platform.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Azure Container Apps overview
Set scaling rules in Azure Container Apps

choices.label: A Container Apps scaling rule appropriate to the workload trigger.
An Azure Files snapshot schedule.
An Azure Policy exemption.
A DNS TXT record.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Scaling rules are the platform-native mechanism.
choice_feedback.B: File snapshots do not scale container replicas.
choice_feedback.C: Policy exemptions do not implement runtime scaling.
choice_feedback.D: DNS records do not scale the application.

question.prompt: Match each Blob access tier to the most appropriate access pattern.
question.explanation: The access tiers trade storage cost against access cost and retrieval characteristics. Archive is offline and must be rehydrated before normal reads.

question.prompt: Both backend VMs are running, but an Azure Load Balancer marks them unhealthy. The health probe targets TCP port 8080, while the application now listens only on TCP 8081. What should you change?
question.explanation: Load Balancer health probes determine whether a backend instance is eligible for new flows. A probe that targets the wrong port will fail even when the application is healthy on another port.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Azure Load Balancer health probes
Azure Load Balancer overview

choices.label: Update the health probe to test the port on which the application is actually listening.
Create a management group above the subscription.
Enable Blob versioning.
Assign Reader to the VMs.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. The probe must test a reachable service endpoint.
choice_feedback.B: Management groups do not affect probe health.
choice_feedback.C: Blob versioning is unrelated.
choice_feedback.D: Reader authorization does not change probe traffic.

question.explanation: Azure Policy evaluates resource compliance, locks protect against modification or deletion, tags attach metadata, and Azure RBAC controls authorization.

question.prompt: A production App Service app must call a private database endpoint reachable only from a virtual network. The app itself should remain publicly accessible. Which App Service networking feature should you use for the app's outbound connection?
question.explanation: App Service virtual network integration enables outbound access from the app into a virtual network. It does not by itself make the app private for inbound traffic.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Networking features in Azure App Service

choices.label: Virtual network integration.
A public Azure Load Balancer frontend for the database.
A resource lock on the app.
Blob object replication.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. VNet integration is the outbound connectivity feature.
choice_feedback.B: Publishing the database through a public load balancer defeats the private-connectivity requirement.
choice_feedback.C: A lock does not provide network connectivity.
choice_feedback.D: Object replication is a storage feature.

question.explanation: Site Recovery is configured before an incident, replication health is monitored, failover is initiated when recovery is needed, and the recovered environment is validated before the recovery is finalized.

question.prompt: A VNet peering link exists between VNet-A and VNet-B. VNet-B is also peered with VNet-C. No other connectivity is configured. Can VM-A reach VM-C automatically through VNet-B solely because both peerings exist?
question.explanation: Azure virtual network peering is not transitive. Peering A-to-B and B-to-C does not automatically create A-to-C connectivity.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Virtual network peering

choices.label: Yes. VNet peering is transitive by default.
No. VNet peering is not transitive; additional routing/connectivity is required.

choice_feedback.A: Peering does not automatically transit traffic through the intermediate VNet.
choice_feedback.B: Correct. A separate peering or routing design is needed.

question.prompt: An administrator wants better recovery options after accidental Blob overwrites and accidental container deletion. Which TWO features directly address these two risks?
question.explanation: Blob versioning preserves previous blob versions after writes, while container soft delete can recover a deleted container during the retention period.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Blob versioning
Soft delete for containers

choices.label: Blob versioning for overwritten blob content.
Container soft delete for deleted containers.
A public IP address on the storage account.
An Azure Policy exemption.
An App Service deployment slot.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Versioning provides previous versions of changed blobs.
choice_feedback.B: Correct. Container soft delete protects container deletion.
choice_feedback.C: Public IP configuration does not protect data history.
choice_feedback.D: A Policy exemption does not create recoverable data copies.
choice_feedback.E: Deployment slots apply to App Service, not Blob protection.

question.prompt: A team deploys a new App Service version to a staging slot, validates it, and then swaps the slot into production. Why is this approach preferable to deploying directly to production?
question.explanation: Deployment slots provide separate deployment environments and support swapping a tested version into production, which reduces risk compared with overwriting production directly.

source_refs.title: Study guide for Exam AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator
Set up staging environments in Azure App Service

choices.label: It supports validation in a separate slot and can reduce release risk during the production swap.
It automatically converts the web app into a VM Scale Set.
It replaces the need for a TLS certificate.
It prevents all future configuration changes with a resource lock.

choice_feedback.A: Correct. Staged deployment and swap are the core benefits.
choice_feedback.B: Slots do not convert App Service to VMs.
choice_feedback.C: TLS requirements remain independent.
choice_feedback.D: Deployment slots are not resource locks.
